title: PrejSense
full_title: PrejSense: Non-intrusive Gaze-Informed Prediction of Implicit Prejudice Against Machine for Proactive Interface Adaptation
author: Gao, Entong and Chen, Zhe
venue_full: Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
summary: Gaze-informed, proactive interface adaptation for human–AI collaboration.
description: PrejSense investigates how gaze signals can inform an estimate of implicit prejudice against AI. The system combines an interpretable prediction model with an LLM-based agent that adapts its interaction strategies, connecting behavioral sensing to proactive interface support.
limitation: This is a proof-of-concept system. Its preliminary user study involved 17 participants; larger-scale validation remains necessary.

figures.caption: Overview of PrejSense in the human–AI collaboration loop.
The research framework, from gaze-based prediction to proactive interface adaptation.

title: UEQManager
full_title: UEQManager: A Non-intrusive and Real-time System for Recognizing and Managing UEQ in Multilingual Voice Assistants
author: Gao, Entong and Yuan, Haisu and Zhong, Hanyu and Yuan, Ruiqing and Chen, Zhe
venue_full: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
summary: Recognizing and supporting user experience in multilingual voice interaction.
description: UEQManager explores a non-intrusive approach to recognizing user experience quality during interaction with multilingual voice assistants. It connects behavioral and physiological signals, interpretable modeling, and adaptive agent strategies in a real-time system.

figures.caption: Research framework linking user experience recognition with adaptive interaction.
A user case illustrating the interface and adaptive support.

title: Multilingual voice interaction under noise
full_title: Multi-Language Intelligent Voice Interaction Under Noise: How the Noise Type and Signal-to-Noise Ratio Shape Comprehension Performance, Pupil Activity and User Experience Quality
summary: How noise type and signal-to-noise ratio shape comprehension and user experience.
description: This study examines multilingual voice interaction under different noise types and signal-to-noise ratios. Comprehension measures, pupil activity, and user experience assessments provide complementary views of how people process voice-based information in challenging listening conditions.

title: “Your Eyes Show It”
full_title: “How Do You Understand? Your Eyes Show It”: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Cross-Language Comprehension Prediction Through Eye Movement
author: Gao, Entong and Zhong, Hanyu and Yuan, Ruiqing and Guo, Jialu and Chen, Zhe
award: Best Paper Award · Cross-Cultural Design, HCII 2025
summary: Explainable AI for cross-language comprehension prediction through eye movement.
description: This work studies eye movement as a signal of comprehension in native and nonnative language settings. It combines predictive modeling and explainable AI with experiments on how AI agents can adapt interaction strategies to users’ comprehension.

title: Comprehension & user experience
full_title: How does comprehension affect user experience quality in multilanguage voice-activated intelligent education?
author: Gao, Entong and Liu, Yun and Zhou, Yage and Guo, Jialu and Chen, Zhe
summary: Understanding the relationship between comprehension and experience in voice-based learning.
description: This research investigates comprehension and user experience quality in multilingual voice-activated intelligent education. It considers both subjective understanding and objective performance, connecting the design of voice interaction to users’ learning experiences.

title: AI companionship during driving
full_title: Exploring the Effects of an AI Voice Assistant on Drivers’ Loneliness and Affect During Long-Distance Driving Under Partial Driving Automation
summary: Studying loneliness, social support, and affect during partially automated driving.
description: This study examines an AI voice assistant in the context of long-distance driving under partial automation. A driving simulator study considers perceived social support, loneliness, and affect, alongside drivers’ accounts of their experience with the assistant.

Estimated marginal means of perceived social support under different experimental conditions. Error bars are standard errors of the means.

title: Voice communication in emergencies

title: Strategic patenting & technological evolution
full_title: Strategic Patenting and Technological Evolution in Energy Utilization and Recovery
summary: Patent analytics for understanding the evolution of energy utilization and recovery technologies.
description: This work studies technological evolution in energy utilization and recovery using patent data. It combines technology classification, network analysis, and machine learning to examine development trajectories and the structure of innovation in the field.
note: 2026 journal issue; first published online in 2025.
